races.name: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Tarriance
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field and sole likely leader; OR 105 gives him class leverage, Colin Keane's positional intelligence will be key, and his Goodwood win over 14f on Good confirms course-and-distance aptitude — although 78 days between runs and a recent mixed form string (17-385) introduce a fitness question over this longer 1m6f trip.

runners_data.name: Align The Stars
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's five-year-old holds two wins over 1m6f at Sandown but has yet to show that Goodwood suits; Daniel Muscutt rides in headgear (p) and a hold-up style means he needs the pace to be genuine — recent form shows a win at Sandown followed by a sixth here, suggesting the course may blunt his effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Burdett Road
runners_data.note: James Owen's six-year-old hold-up type has the benefit of Mason Paetel's 5lb claim but his Goodwood record is underwhelming (six runs, one placed finish), and a form string of 293706 over 12-16f at this course signals a horse that struggles to land the blow even when conditions align.

runners_data.name: Hopewell Rock
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for George Boughey on this four-year-old who stays prominent and has placed twice in similar conditions over 10-12f on soft — the step up to 1m6f on Good to Firm is an open question, though Moore's positioning skill makes him a natural danger from just off the pace.

runners_data.name: Stressfree
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand's mount has a win over 12f on Good here and prominent-style form that suits the likely race shape; David O'Meara's stable has been ticking over (5/50 in 14 days) and 46 days since last run is a minor query, though recent Goodwood form reads reasonably for this trip and surface.

runners_data.name: Nesthorn
runners_data.note: George Baker's hold-up four-year-old has produced seven consecutive finishes between 4th and 7th at Goodwood and simply cannot find a way to win — the form line (-77774) over 9-12f tells a story of a horse that gets into contention but lacks the necessary finishing gear to convert.

runners_data.name: Aeronautic
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's five-year-old carries headgear (t) and has placed three times over Goodwood 12-14f prominently, suggesting course form is credible; Dylan Browne McMonagle is a strong booking and 46 days between runs is not damaging, but the drop to OR 97 from a horse that ran 4th-6th in similar company limits upside.

runners_data.name: Nightime Dancer
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's four-year-old wears a hood (b) and has recorded two fourth-place finishes over Goodwood 13-14f, keeping him consistently thereabouts without converting; Sean Levey has a 0W3P record in similar-going at this venue and the prominent style fits the race shape, but the consistent near-miss profile is a concern.

runners_data.name: Sing Us A Song
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's four-year-old has a win over 14f on Soft and a second over 12f at Goodwood in recent form; James Doyle's positional awareness is a tactical asset from a prominent berth, and this horse's profile — staying-bred, suited by ease in the ground but competitive on Good — makes it a genuine player in the dominant scenario.

runners_data.name: Valedictory
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's four-year-old is a genuine front-runner on a hat-trick, with three recent wins over 10-14f; William Buick's booking is significant but the horse is mapped further back than its natural style because the field is saturated with prominent types — if Buick does secure a forward position, the class and form make it dangerous, but that starting position is far from assured.

runners_data.name: Too Soon
runners_data.note: Warren Fentiman (3lb claim) partnering Gary & Josh Moore's four-year-old, who has a win over 12f on Soft but zero placed form on Good or better (0/0 in sim-going band); the hold-up style (hg:p) and 56-day break combine to make this a significant each-way risk on a surface that may not bring out the best.

runners_data.name: Bahadur
runners_data.note: S Woods's four-year-old is a natural prominent racer whose previous win came over 1m6f at Goodwood in similar conditions; David Egan rides just 14 days after his last run, which keeps fitness sharp — the horse will want to press forward but finds itself squeezed out of that position by a field full of similar types, reducing its chance of running its race.

runners_data.name: Small Fry
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners Joseph Patrick O'Brien's five-year-old, who has form at 1m6f to 2m6f — including a second over 16f at Goodwood — and is a naturally front-going type; the horse is placed further back on the map than it wants to be given the density of prominent runners, and while the trip and jockey are positive factors, running out of preferred position over this distance is a notable handicap.

runners_data.name: Incensed
runners_data.note: Amanda Perrett's five-year-old has placed form at 12f at Goodwood (3rd, 2nd) and the prominent racing style fits the race shape on paper; the trainer has no runners in the 14-day window (0/4) and the horse's front-going nature is compromised by the field's structural crowding, meaning its natural rhythm is likely disrupted before the race has even found its stride.

races.paceDynamic: Tarriance is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field over 1m6f on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood, and with no credible rival willing to press him early, Colin Keane can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front. Behind him, Hopewell Road, Stressfree, Aeronautic, Nightime Dancer and Sing Us A Song all carry genuine prominent inclinations but are likely to settle in a chasing pack rather than mount an early challenge, meaning the pace is real but not pressured — a rhythm that suits a horse who can switch off and quicken. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the map can accommodate: Valedictory, Bahadur, Small Fry and Incensed are all natural prominent racers who will find themselves racing further back than ideal, with Valedictory (William Buick, Gosden) and Small Fry (Oisin Murphy) most likely to eventually secure a forward berth if any gaps open. With a single horse controlling an honest but uncontested tempo over a stamina trip on fast ground, the race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace who can track the leader into the straight and produce a sustained finish — pure hold-up horses hunting a sprint finish will find the race run too evenly to deliver the late gap they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tarriance Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Tarriance is allowed to dictate an unchallenged but honest gallop and the prominent trackers produce a sustained run in the straight.
scenarios.body: Keane settles Tarriance into an uncontested lead, the pace is fair but not punishing, and the horses racing just behind him into the Goodwood straight get first run; Ryan Moore on Hopewell Rock or James Doyle on Sing Us A Song are ideally placed to pounce with a turning-run finish over this stamina trip. This scenario rewards horses positioned second to fifth who travel smoothly and hit the rising-ground finish with energy in hand.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tarriance Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is conservative enough that Tarriance's class advantage on 105 OR allows him to sustain his lead into the final furlong without being run down.
scenarios.body: Keane, a top-class operator, reads the race perfectly and prolongs the gallop just enough to stretch the field without breaking his own horse; with no rival applying early pressure, Tarriance's prominent racing style at OR 105 becomes a genuine front-running weapon. The hold-up horses arrive too late and the nearest prominent chasers cannot accelerate sharply enough to reel him in on Good to Firm ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely brisk enough — due to Tarriance being chased — to soften the leaders and create a strong closing opportunity.
scenarios.body: Align The Stars or Burdett Road, racing patiently from the rear, find the leaders emptying in the final two furlongs and motor through on a rail or outer; this shape depends on the race being genuinely run, which requires pressure on Tarriance that the current field structure does not guarantee. The probability is tempered by the fact that the most likely closers carry modest recent form and sit well below Align The Stars's best course credentials at Sandown rather than Goodwood.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Strike
scenarios.trigger: If one of the naturally prominent horses — Valedictory or Small Fry — manages to secure a forward berth and turns the race into a test of class from the front.
scenarios.body: Valedictory, trained by Gosden and ridden by Buick, is on a hat-trick and has an OR of 95 that may understate current ability; if Buick presses forward early and claims a prominent position, Valedictory's recent winning form could make it competitive from the front. This shape carries a lower probability because these horses are expected to be shuffled back by the structural weight of prominent runners, meaning they are likely racing out of their natural role.

watchPoints.text: Tarriance — watch whether Colin Keane is challenged for the lead in the first half-mile; if he gets a completely free rail with no rival within three lengths, his ability to control fractions makes him significantly more dangerous than his current odds may reflect.

Valedictory and Small Fry — both are natural front-runners mapped to midfield due to pace congestion; watch at the start whether William Buick or Oisin Murphy push forward aggressively to reclaim their natural position, as a successful move forward would transform either horse's chance.

Hopewell Rock — Ryan Moore's ability to track the leader from second or third is the key tactical variable; if Moore can sit directly on Tarriance's quarters through the first mile, the prominent-style profile is perfectly set up for a Goodwood straight turning finish.

Align The Stars — in a race where the pace may not be brutally strong, this hold-up horse needs Tarriance to go fast enough to soften the prominent chasers; if Tarriance coasts, Align The Stars's late run may arrive at the same time as the tracked runners and lack the length of run to overhaul them.

Nesthorn — seven consecutive Goodwood runs without a win is a clear pattern flag; Benoit de la Sayette has course experience here but punters should note that this horse's form over Goodwood 9-12f has been consistently flat, and there is no strong reason to expect a breakthrough on this occasion.

races.name: Coral Glorious Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Al Aasy
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old still performing with credit, William Haggas and Tom Marquand find him in a race perfectly suited to his prominent, track-the-leader profile; four wins at Goodwood and strong similar-going form (11/15) make him one of the best-qualified horses in the field for today's conditions, and a 28-day break is entirely manageable at his age.

runners_data.name: Enfjaar
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's six-year-old arrives on 46 days off and carries a hood; he wants to race prominently but the congested pace map means he is likely to find himself further back than ideal, which compromises his ability to dictate his own rhythm, and his Goodwood record of 3-3-4-4-5 at 10f suggests he may find 1m4f a touch beyond his best.

runners_data.name: Ghostwriter
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's five-year-old is the race's sole confirmed front-runner and David Egan will exploit that position freely; his recent form string of 0-3-6-4-3 shows he has not won in a while, but controlling a modest tempo on Good to Firm Goodwood where he has strong course familiarity makes him a genuine and dangerous pace factor regardless.

runners_data.name: Involvement
runners_data.note: Simon and Ed Crisford send William Buick on a horse who naturally wants to be prominent, yet with so many pace-hungry rivals, Involvement is likely to find himself racing a position or two further back than suits; his Goodwood form at 12f is decent (third and sixth) and his recent win at 10f shows he is in form, but the tactical compromise is real.

runners_data.name: King's Gambit
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's five-year-old has been in a run of moderate form (6-7-9 at Goodwood) and Jamie Spencer will need to find a prominent pitch that may simply not be available given the crowded front-end; his best efforts came at 9-10f and this 1m4f trip on fast ground may ask an additional question.

runners_data.name: Midak
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' four-year-old is the race's one genuine hold-up horse and ran just 14 days ago; his form (4-4-9-6-4) shows consistent mid-division finishes without threatening to win, and in a race likely to be won by a prominent tracker, he would need an exceptional leap in form to be competitive from his natural rearward berth.

runners_data.name: Opportunity
runners_data.note: William Haggas sends out Opportunity with James Doyle, and his two recent Goodwood wins at 12f on similar ground are the standout course-and-distance credentials in the race; he is a natural prominent racer who will be pushed back from his preferred position by the congested pace map, making it harder for him to travel sweetly, but his class and course form mean he remains a major player if he can work forward.

runners_data.name: In My Teens
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's four-year-old won at Goodwood over 12f last time and Oisin Murphy is an upgrade in the saddle; he carries a hood and has a 34-day break behind him, and while his 9-10-6-7 form at longer trips suggests he is best around this distance rather than further, his natural prominent style is genuinely suited to tracking Ghostwriter in a race where that position is at a premium.

races.paceDynamic: Ghostwriter is the one confirmed front-runner and will stride to the lead from the outset on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood, setting a sustainable and controlled tempo over 1m4f that is unlikely to be seriously pressured. Al Aasy and In My Teens are the genuine prominent types who can sit just off the pace in their natural roles, while Opportunity, King's Gambit, Enfjaar and Involvement are all true prominent racers who cannot all occupy their preferred position and will be shuffled back further than ideal. This field carries significant pace congestion — Opportunity, King's Gambit, Enfjaar and Involvement are natural front-of-field horses mapped to midfield positions they would not voluntarily choose, meaning the race shape is likely less pressured than the head count suggests. With Ghostwriter controlling a moderate tempo from the front and the genuine closers thin on the ground, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in behind the leader and quicken off a steady gallop — the prominent racer who tracks Ghostwriter most smoothly holds the decisive tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ghostwriter Leads, Prompters Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Ghostwriter dictates an uncontested, measured tempo and the race is won by a horse tracking in second or third.
scenarios.body: Ghostwriter rolls along at a comfortable clip on Good to Firm Goodwood and the horses sitting closest to the pace have first run at the two-furlong pole; those with a prominent natural style who actually secure a tracking berth benefit most from the clean passage and the steady early fractions that preserve energy for a sustained finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Injected Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed prominent types — Opportunity or King's Gambit — pushes forward earlier than mapped and lifts the tempo, turning the race into a genuine test.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop stretches the field and makes it harder for Ghostwriter to conserve for a late kick, opening the door for a horse with superior class and stamina to stay on when others flatten out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Ghostwriter Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Ghostwriter is never headed and the pace is slow enough that none of the tracking horses can accelerate past in the straight.
scenarios.body: On a flat, fast Goodwood track with a benign pace, Ghostwriter dictates the fractions and simply out-gallops a disorganised chasing group that never gets properly organised behind; a front-runner who controls its own rhythm on Good to Firm turf can prove very hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or horses fall back en masse, creating a vacuum that allows Midak or another rearward horse to finish fastest of all.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on a truly dysfunctional early pace and Midak running to a markedly higher level than recent form suggests — both conditions are low probability given the controlled front-runner and the quality of the tracking horses.

watchPoints.text: Opportunity — if James Doyle pushes forward before the race settles and bypasses his mapped midfield position, the entire pace topology shifts and Ghostwriter faces genuine competition for the lead from a horse with superior Goodwood course-and-distance form.

Al Aasy is nine years old and while his record at Goodwood is outstanding, watch for any sign at the start or in the early stages that he is not travelling with his usual fluency — a horse of his age can decline sharply between runs.

In My Teens wore a hood and Cromwell's string is cold (T14: 0/34) — monitor paddock demeanour and whether Murphy can get him racing prominently enough to exploit what is otherwise an ideal race shape for his style.

Ghostwriter has not won since 2023 despite frequent prominent positions; if he is picked off between the two-furlong and one-furlong poles rather than at the line, it confirms he is losing his finishing effort rather than simply being outclassed — a meaningful form reading for future races.

The Good to Firm going is confirmed for this race specifically — horses with strong similar-going records (Al Aasy 4W7P, Opportunity 3W4P at sim going) hold a measurable advantage over those whose profiles are less tested on fast ground.

races.name: Qatar Lillie Langtry Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Santorini Star
runners_data.note: Course winner (Goodwood, 12f) and placed here over 16f, this five-year-old's form figures on similar going read 4W4P from seven runs — a high-class profile that suits sitting just off Danielle and unwinding a sustained challenge; Tom Marquand rides for the in-form Haggas stable and the 1m6f trip is well within range.

runners_data.name: Consent
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's four-year-old won last time at Haydock over 14f and has placed twice over this longer trip on soft, but her lone similar-going run at Goodwood produced a win (10f, Good) — 72 days off may mean peak fitness, and Luke Morris will slot her prominently behind the leader where this race is likely to be decided.

runners_data.name: Danielle
runners_data.note: Wins her last two starts including a course-and-distance victory at Goodwood and a Haydock win on good, confirming she goes well fresh (70 days); Buick will likely dictate from the front and the STYLE_FIT flag is relevant only insofar as she is shown as prominent on the map — her natural role here is uncontested leader, which is exactly what she'll be.

runners_data.name: Goodie Two Shoes
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's seven-year-old is in truth a front-running or prominent-racing type who has won at 14f on good and placed at this Goodwood 14f — but with more prominent horses than space allows, Dylan Browne McMonagle may find her unable to secure her natural berth and forced to race in an unfamiliar midfield position; STYLE_FIT of 0.92 tempers confidence accordingly.

runners_data.name: Little Dorrit
runners_data.note: The lone genuine hold-up runner in this field, Roger Varian's four-year-old has five Goodwood runs to her name without a win and has been beaten out of the frame in all five — a structural disadvantage in a slow-pace scenario, and an OR of 96 looks modest at Group 2 level even with Ray Dawson claiming an allowance.

runners_data.name: Waardah
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows' four-year-old won twice earlier in the season over 10f and 14f on soft and has placed on good at Goodwood (11f) — genuinely a forward-going type who wants to race prominently, but the crowded front ranks mean she is likely to be carried back into a midfield position that doesn't suit; T14 shows 0 wins from 8 runners is a negative trainer angle.

runners_data.name: Amelia Earhart
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's three-year-old won twice at Goodwood (8f and 12f, Good) and shaped with promise before finishing fifth in a deeper 12f race here last time — Ryan Moore is a major positive, she wears a hood (headgear noted), and her age and lighter weight of 125lbs are interesting, but she is a natural front-rank type reshuffled to midfield by a crowded pace map which limits confidence at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Danielle is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to pressure her from the outside, William Buick can dictate terms at a measured, controlled gallop over Goodwood's 1m6f on good-to-firm ground. That sustainable pace is likely to suit horses who can sit close to the leader and produce a decisive move in the straight rather than those needing a truly searching gallop to reel the field in. Santorini Star and Consent are both natural prominent racers who should be able to slot in just behind Danielle and use that proximity productively, making the race shape one that rewards front-rank runners with finishing speed. The field holds more prominent-minded horses than the pace map can accommodate: Goodie Two Shoes, Waardah, and Amelia Earhart are all genuine forwardly-placed types but at least some of them will be shuffled back into unfamiliar midfield positions in a seven-runner contest with a single true leader, diluting their chances of expressing their natural style. **Tactical verdict: this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently in second or third, combining positional advantage with a tactical turn of foot — hold-up horses relying on a strong, relentless gallop are at a structural disadvantage.**

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Danielle Controls, Proximity Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Danielle leads at a controlled tempo and the race is truly run to suit horses settled close to the pace.
scenarios.body: Buick nurses Danielle to the home turn without serious challenge, and the runners positioned just behind — Santorini Star and Consent — use their proximity to mount the most credible attacks in the straight; stragglers from midfield simply have too little fuel burnt to get home in time.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Quickening Straight
scenarios.trigger: If Danielle's controlled gallop produces a sprint finish and a horse with sharp acceleration ambushes the field late.
scenarios.body: The steady pace compresses the field into a tight bunch entering the straight and a horse with an explosive turn of foot benefits most; Goodie Two Shoes, if managing to sit closer than her mapped position suggests, could capitalise on the sprint scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals Race
scenarios.trigger: If Danielle is allowed to build such an unchallenged lead that no horse from mid-division can close the gap.
scenarios.body: With a field of just seven and minimal pressure, Buick could exploit the slow fractions to steal lengths from the home turn, and Danielle's recent course-and-distance win at Goodwood on similar ground suggests she possesses the stamina reserves to hold on if the effort is timed correctly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and genuine hold-up types find sufficient gallop to overpower the front rank.
scenarios.body: Little Dorrit is the only true hold-up runner in the field, but her record at this track (five runs, zero wins) and an OR of 96 against Group 2 rivals makes this scenario a low-probability outcome even if conditions conspire in her favour; Waardah closing from midfield would also require an uncharacteristically strong tempo.

watchPoints.text: Danielle's ability to set an uncontested, unchallenged gallop is the single biggest race-shaping factor — if Buick elects to go very steady, watch for the entire field queuing up behind her and proximity to the pace becoming the decisive edge.

Goodie Two Shoes, Waardah, and Amelia Earhart are all genuine prominent types competing for positions that only one or two can occupy — early crowding or jostling for spots behind Danielle in the first half-mile could compromise all three and disrupt their rhythm significantly.

Consent's 72-day absence for Sir Mark Prescott is worth monitoring in the paddock — Prescott runners returning from a lengthy break are often primed, but it is not guaranteed, and any fitness shortfall at 1m6f on a testing finish could see her fade in the straight.

Little Dorrit has been placed at 12f on soft repeatedly but never won at Goodwood in five attempts — watch whether she makes any ground at all in the straight, as her hold-up style is structurally ill-suited to the controlled pace Danielle is expected to set.

Going is Good to Firm throughout the card at Goodwood today — any horse whose best form comes on a softer surface (notably Consent, who has multiple soft-ground placings) should be monitored for whether the faster ground blunts their finish.

races.name: Coral Stewards' Cup (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Soldier's Tree
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner; has finished third three times in a row at Goodwood over 6f on similar going, so the track and trip are clearly suited, but a win has been elusive and the weight of 138lbs is a concern — Mason Paetel's 5lb claim is the key mitigant; tagged STYLE_FIT as a Prominent, but here it is genuinely in its natural lead role.

runners_data.name: Dubai Bling
runners_data.note: William Buick takes over and that is a significant booking — three wins from 13 runs on Good/Good to Firm at Goodwood and goes well fresh (21 days); proven 6f performer at this course with a visor, and a horse that secures a clean prominent position early will be very well placed in this pace map.

runners_data.name: Northern Champion
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a hat-trick of Goodwood wins and an excellent record on quick ground at this track; 135lbs is a big ask for a three-year-old but Ashley Lewis's 5lb claim offsets some of that, and a horse with this course form is extremely dangerous when the pace is controlled.

runners_data.name: Mitbaahy
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who likes a tongue tie and has a solid Goodwood record at 6f; Jamie Spencer is a master at getting horses to settle and conserve energy, which is crucial given the crowded prominent group — goes on Good to Firm and 14 days since last run suits.

runners_data.name: West Acre
runners_data.note: 183 days off the track is the obvious concern, though the 2025 record at Goodwood (placed) is encouraging; wears a hood and tends to race prominently over 5-6f here — the layoff is the key question mark and needs to hit the ground running immediately.

runners_data.name: Sondad
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer by nature but mapped to midfield here because the field is over-supplied with horses who want that position; wears a visor and has won twice at Goodwood over 6f in similar conditions — strong form figures at this track but getting trapped wide or behind early would be damaging.

runners_data.name: Run Boy Run
runners_data.note: Ran only four days ago, which is the headline concern; wears a visor and is a horse that needs things to go right early — the 12/15 placed runs on similar going shows the going is not an issue but the quick turnaround from Goodwood four days back is a risk.

runners_data.name: Two Tribes
runners_data.note: Second in the Stewards' Cup last year gives this one major claims — wears a hood and has a consistent Goodwood profile; David Egan rides and the horse has a clean record at 7f at Goodwood, stepping back to 6f here is the only slight query.

runners_data.name: Get It
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who has won at Goodwood before at 6f on this going and is a genuine hold-up horse — 314 days off the track is a massive flag and the comeback run form (14th at Sandown) does nothing to inspire confidence despite the impressive historical record.

runners_data.name: Completely Random
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes over and the horse won over 6f on soft going — this Good to Firm is firmer than ideal and the 9/15 placed record on similar going reflects some vulnerability; though with Moore aboard and a prominent tendency, expect to be produced prominently regardless.

runners_data.name: Garfield Shadow
runners_data.note: Consistent placegetter at Goodwood over 6f with a 2/6f/GOO and 3/6f/GOO in recent history — Harry Vigors (5lb claim) is an upside, and the horse has won here before; the 6-from-10 placed record at Goodwood makes it live if it handles the top of the draw.

runners_data.name: Tuco Salamanca
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner by inclination who cannot get that position in this race; Dylan Browne McMonagle is a significant jockey booking and the horse won over 6f at Sandown and Wolverhampton recently — but the 5/15 Goodwood-going placed rate hints at this track not suiting as well.

runners_data.name: Stratusnine
runners_data.note: Won over 6f at Goodwood last time out and has a course-winning profile that is hard to ignore; Hugo Palmer fields two here and this one has the better recent form — naturally wants to be up with the pace, but being forced to sit further back in a big field could compromise its chance.

runners_data.name: Annaf
runners_data.note: Daniel Muscutt partners this genuine hold-up type with a modest placed record on similar going (1P from 10); seven-year-old who rarely wins anymore but is consistent, and the hold-up style is correctly mapped — not expected to win but the style is authentic.

runners_data.name: Invictus Gold
runners_data.note: Placed over 6f at Goodwood on soft going and has a reasonable record at this track; Jason Watson rides and the horse has the pace profile to find a clean position just off the leaders if the field compresses — 33 days fresh is fine.

runners_data.name: Fandom
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's five-year-old is a genuine stalker who races prominently but the over-supplied pace map means it will likely sit in a squeezed midfield; the 10/12 placed record on similar going shows it handles conditions, and Sean Levey is a reliable pilot — one win at this course in recent form.

runners_data.name: Far Above Dream
runners_data.note: Kieran Shoemark partners a horse with four wins from 14 at Goodwood on good-to-firm-type going — the four wins in this year alone are striking; naturally wants to be prominent but is displaced in the pace map, meaning it must find a gap late from a position it does not prefer.

runners_data.name: Hammer The Hammer
runners_data.note: A Toby Moore (7lb claim) pilot on a horse whose last five runs show 14th, 14th, 16th, 6th and 5th — the form is poor and the going appears fine, but this horse has struggled in big fields at Goodwood before and the weight/form combination is discouraging.

runners_data.name: Realign
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained four-year-old with two wins at 6f on good-equivalent going; Tom Marquand is a strong booking but 42 days off and a displaced prominent style in this field means it will need things to fall right — the OR of 98 and form figures suggest it is better than its current mark but the race shape may not suit.

runners_data.name: Flash Harry
runners_data.note: A Clive Cox four-year-old who wants to be up with the pace by nature but is mapped further back given field congestion; the 6/8 placed record at Goodwood on similar going is modest, and the form string (310-60) does not inspire confidence for a competitive handicap of this magnitude.

runners_data.name: Berkshire Whisper
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes over for Andrew Balding but 77 days off is a red flag for a horse that has not won on Good to Firm at Goodwood in five attempts; the 0/12 win record on similar going says enough — only consistent placed form at Sandown, not here.

runners_data.name: Candy
runners_data.note: Callum Hutchinson rides a horse that ran only four days ago — like stablemate Run Boy Run, the quick turnaround is a concern; a genuine hold-up type that won on soft at Carlisle but has been 23rd and 27th at Goodwood previously, suggesting the track does not suit.

runners_data.name: Ferrous
runners_data.note: Natural prominent racer pushed into the midfield section of the map by pace congestion; Callum Rodriguez rides for Jack Channon and the horse has two seconds at Goodwood over 6f, but the 0/15 win record on similar going and a displaced position are both working against it.

runners_data.name: King Of Light
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani partners a four-year-old who won over 6f at Goodwood on good ground earlier in the season — that course win is the key positive; however, naturally displaced into midfield in this overcrowded field and the OR drop to 91 is significant.

runners_data.name: Dark Thirty
runners_data.note: Jason Hart rides for John & Sean Quinn — four wins from 15 at Goodwood at 6f on this going and a form string that reads 710212, including recent victories, is very compelling form for this race; a genuinely prominent-type horse who by nature wants to be in that position and has the course record to support it.

runners_data.name: Evening Saigon
runners_data.note: James Doyle is a strong booking for Hamad Al Jehani and this four-year-old won over 6f at Goodwood and Sandown in 2024 — but only 3/8 placed on similar going is modest, and 42 days off combined with a displaced prominent profile in a 28-runner field makes the race shape difficult.

runners_data.name: Gold Star Hero
runners_data.note: Hector Crouch rides a Michael Bell horse with three wins from five at Goodwood on good equivalent going — the win record (1/5f/STA, 1/6f/STA, 1/6f/STA) is impressive but those were at Sandown,

races.paceDynamic: Soldier's Tree is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only one horse genuinely happy to lead, they will set a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than a pressured, helter-skelter pace — on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood this is a significant tactical factor. Behind them, Dubai Bling, Northern Champion, Mitbaahy, West Acre, Run Boy Run, Two Tribes and Completely Random all want to race prominently, meaning the early positions directly behind the leader will be fiercely contested and many of these horses will end up racing slightly off their preferred pitch. The field is saturated with prominent types — Ferrous, Far Above Dream, Fandom, Tuco Salamanca, Stratusnine, Berkshire Whisper, Flash Harry, Realign and others are all natural stalkers who simply cannot all slot in where they want, compressing the field into a tight bunch through the middle stages. With one honest but uncontested gallop-setter, a tightly packed prominent group racing slightly off their best ground positionally, and fast Good to Firm conditions, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel smoothly in the first half of the race and quicken in the final two furlongs — genuinely prominent types who secure a clean position just off Soldier's Tree, rather than hold-up runners who must pick through a wall of horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent holds on, wins
scenarios.trigger: If Soldier's Tree sets a fair but not pressured clip and the horses who secure a front-rank position just behind can quicken on the Good to Firm surface.
scenarios.body: The compressed, single-pacesetter dynamic means those who get a clean position in the first three or four places will save ground, avoid traffic and have the first run — on fast Goodwood ground this translates directly into a winning advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader's companions flatten out
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to stretch the field and the prominent group tires in the final furlong, leaving space for a well-positioned midfield horse to pick up.
scenarios.body: Horses like Completely Random or Invictus Gold, who can sit a touch off the early fractions and still be travelling when others are tying up, would be the chief beneficiaries here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers swoop late
scenarios.trigger: If the contested positions behind Soldier's Tree force a stronger-than-expected tempo and the front group burns out in the last 100 yards.
scenarios.body: The few genuine hold-up horses — Get It, Annaf, Toca Madera, Candy — would be the only real winners in this scenario, as they are not competing for early position and will arrive fresh at the death.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, wide draw prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the race fragments due to crowding and jostling for position on the rail, with horses getting hampered or impeded mid-race on the way down the straight.
scenarios.body: Redistributed prominent types like Dark Thirty or Far Above Dream, who have strong Goodwood form and proven ability to find room on this track, could capitalise if circumstances force a more strung-out race.

races.name: Phase Eight Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Wild Desert
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's progressive three-year-old has won twice at Goodwood including over this course and distance; a confirmed front-runner in great hands with Buick, he handles good to firm well (4/5 on similar going) though his last run at Goodwood was a below-par sixth — may be sharp enough to front-run and outclass these.

runners_data.name: Aqpan
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's hold-up type is one of only two genuinely off-the-pace runners in this field; 70 days off is a notable concern, and his recent form includes defeats at 6f on soft and good at Goodwood, but his two form figures on similar tracks (1st and 2nd at Sandown) give hope if this turns into a true gallop.

runners_data.name: We're Goosers
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's colt has already won twice at Goodwood, including over 7f, and Oisin Murphy is a significant booking; a natural prominent racer who should secure a good position from the off, though a 30th at the July meeting is a worry — course form and jockey upgrade make him interesting.

runners_data.name: Utmost Good Faith
runners_data.note: One of the two genuine hold-up types here; won at Goodwood 31 days ago over this distance and trip form is solid, handling good ground well (2 wins from 6 runs on similar surfaces); Stuart Williams' runner could be tailor-made if tempo lifts and closers are rewarded.

runners_data.name: Ghost Mode
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's colt wants to race prominently but has been winless on good or good to firm ground at Goodwood in his last four attempts here; stepping up from 6f, and the distance question over 7f on fast ground must be respected despite Rob Hornby's positive booking.

runners_data.name: Egoli
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's visor-equipped three-year-old won at Goodwood 14 days ago over this course and distance — the freshest winning course form in the race; David Egan continues the partnership and Egoli's strong Goodwood record (3 wins from 9 runs on similar going) makes this runner's prominent style highly effective here.

runners_data.name: Naval Light
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's consistent performer has won back-to-back, including over this course and distance 17 days ago; Jack Nicholls (3) takes the ride and the form line of 3-3-8-1-1 on similar ground is compelling — a natural prominent racer with a strong each-way profile in this shape.

runners_data.name: Ironwill
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams has the two-strong team here; this colt's natural instinct is to race prominently, but with so many rivals chasing that ground, Ironwill is likely to find himself further back than ideal — a genuine frontrunner's profile squeezed into a race that may not allow him to express it, though two Goodwood wins suggest course aptitude.

runners_data.name: Proud Nation
runners_data.note: Fahey's runner has two placed efforts and a win at Goodwood over 7f and wants to race close to the pace; in this traffic-heavy field he is likely to be bumped back further than his form requires — the redistribution tempers his chance, though his course and distance credentials remain legitimate if he can secure a good slot.

runners_data.name: Startled
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes' runner has won twice over 7f at Goodwood and is a genuine prominent racer; with 49 days since last running and the crowded prominent berths ahead of him, his natural position will be hard to achieve — the Goodwood form is real, but the race shape works against him unless he can find space early in the straight.

runners_data.name: Marengo Storm
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes also runs Marengo Storm, who won last time out over 7f at Goodwood and wears a visor; in a field of this prominence-density he too is unlikely to get the prominent position that suits him, and the trainer's two-runner situation with Startled adds a further complication — course form is there, but circumstances are against.

runners_data.name: Start Me Up
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer's runner wears a hood and has won over 7f at Goodwood; his natural style suits racing close to the pace but this congested field pushes him back, and with only a 2/21 trainer 14-day strike rate the stable is not firing at the same level as rivals — his best chance depends on others making mistakes.

runners_data.name: Ay Up Duck
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's lowest-rated runner in the field won at Goodwood over 7f most recently and is only 9 days fresh; despite course form, the weight of superior rivals and the near-certainty of a position further back than ideal means he faces a stiff task — Nicola Currie will need everything to go right.

races.paceDynamic: Wild Desert is the one confirmed front-runner and, with William Buick in the saddle for Charlie Appleby, is highly likely to stride on and set a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood's 7f. Behind him, the prominent berths are fiercely contested: Egoli, Naval Light, We're Goosers, Ghost Mode and Ironwill all want to race close to the pace, meaning several will be squeezed back into positions that do not suit their natural style. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically secure their preferred position — Wild Desert and Egoli (equipped with a visor, progressive at this course) look most likely to actually hold the front two positions, with Naval Light and Ghost Mode scrapping for the next slots and Ironwill, Proud Nation, Startled, Marengo Storm, Start Me Up and Ay Up Duck all forced to race wider or deeper than ideal. With Wild Desert dictating an honest but unforced pace on fast ground, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race handily just off the leader or who possess a genuine turn of foot to pick off a legitimate pace — prominent-to-midfield closers with proven Goodwood form are the primary beneficiaries, while true hold-up types Aqpan and Utmost Good Faith are the only runners in genuine off-the-pace positions to capitalise if the pace collapses late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wild Desert Controls, Handy Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Desert sets a fair but manageable pace and those racing prominently just behind him get the clearest runs into the Goodwood straight.
scenarios.body: Wild Desert dictates from the front on good to firm ground he handles well, but the race is run at a tempo that sets up those racing second or third to pick off the leader in the final furlong; Egoli's visor and recent Goodwood winning form, and Naval Light's back-to-back wins including over this course and distance, make both prime beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Increases, Closers Sweep Through
scenarios.trigger: If the congested early battle for prominent positions pushes the tempo high enough to compromise the leaders from the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace from the outset — caused by multiple horses competing for prominent ground — strings the field out and sees the prominent runners tire inside the final furlong; Utmost Good Faith, who has recent winning form at this course and is a natural hold-up type, and Aqpan, the other genuine off-the-pace runner, are best positioned to sweep past beaten rivals late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Wild Desert Dictates and Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely steady and no challenger can muster the acceleration to reel in a well-positioned front-runner on fast ground.
scenarios.body: Wild Desert has already won over this course and distance and loves Goodwood, and a soft, controlled gallop under Buick means energy is conserved for a prolonged gallop home; this shape suits the leader who is already in his comfort zone, with We're Goosers the most likely to chase him home having also won here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Outsiders Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded prominent group causes interference or checks in running that shuffle the finishing order unpredictably.
scenarios.body: With so many horses out of their natural position and jostling for space on the tight Goodwood track, a check or squeeze mid-race could promote a horse who finds clean air at the right moment; Startled and Proud Nation, both true prominent types forced further back than ideal, retain some chance if they find daylight early in the straight.

watchPoints.text: Egoli — won here 14 days ago with the visor and is one of the few prominent types likely to actually secure that position; if she leads or tracks Wild Desert closely, she is the primary danger.
Naval Light — back-to-back wins including over this course and distance just 17 days ago; if he gets a clear prominent pitch behind Wild Desert the form reads better than his OR suggests.

Prominence battle in the first two furlongs — Ironwill, Proud Nation, Startled, Ghost Mode and Marengo Storm all want early position and cannot all have it; watch for crowding or checks in the first two furlongs that could compromise several fancies.

Utmost Good Faith — one of only two true hold-up horses; if the pace is steady rather than strong, her off-the-pace run will not be rewarded, so monitor how the early tempo develops before assessing her chances.

Wild Desert's last run — his sixth at Goodwood last time represents a notable backward step for a Appleby/Buick runner; watch whether he jumps cleanly and settles into the lead, as any sign of reluctance to lead may open the race up considerably.

races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Maiden Stakes (Colts And Geldings Only)
Coral Rewards Shaker Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rock Of Cashel
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Jamie Spencer who has placed twice in similar Goodwood going; drops back to 1m1f which suits better than 1m4f-1m6f runs suggest, and 44 days off is fine, but Spencer must find room in a packed straight from a back-of-field position.

runners_data.name: Alpha Crucis
runners_data.note: Has headgear (p) and all five recent runs on soft-ish ground — just one placing from 15 comparable-going starts is a serious flag on today's Good to Firm; Jason Watson takes over for Gary & Moore but the going is the dominant concern here.

runners_data.name: Boyfriend
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon yard firing at 12/59 over 14 days and Pat Dobbs knows this horse; 14 runs on Goodwood Good-to-Firm going with two wins and six places is an exceptional course-and-conditions record that makes him a primary candidate in any prominent-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Real Gain
runners_data.note: James Doyle gets on a horse with seven wins or places from 13 similar-going runs; held up slightly on the wide side at times but can travel prominent and his Goodwood form (five recent runs here) gives confidence at the track despite 86 days off.

runners_data.name: El Matador
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's 4yo has been placed in four of last five and goes well on Goodwood going (4/10 in similar); Hector Crouch can slot him just off the leader where he clearly thrives, and the step back up from 7f-8f to 9f should suit his stamina-tinged profile.

runners_data.name: Ammes
runners_data.note: Carries hood (v) and has form at Goodwood over 10f and 12f on Good; stepping back to 9f is a slight unknown on profile but James Owen is operating at 18/50 over 14 days, and Kieran Shoemark booked is a positive — 10 similar-going runs show three wins.

runners_data.name: Spell Master
runners_data.note: Won at Sandown 7f on Standard and placed on Goodwood Going — Oli Rix yard has just 1/5 over 14 days; the 21-day turnaround is fine and Ray Dawson retains the ride, but the form string shows inconsistency (8th in Goodwood 10f last time) and there is no clear edge.

runners_data.name: Nostrum
runners_data.note: Tagged as fading in the finish and all five recent runs confirm that tendency; Michael Appleby's 6yo drops to 1m1f but the going-form (0W2P from 11 similar) and the fade flag make him hard to back even from a midfield draw in this shape.

runners_data.name: Sweet Reward
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's 9yo is a genuine front-running/prominent type who has won twice and placed five times in 15 comparable-going races; Rob Hornby partners him and he is experienced enough to push forward and claim a position despite the crowded early stages — the style-fit discount applies but his race-craft is real.

runners_data.name: Point Of Contact
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy on a 4yo trained by Andrew Balding who has won twice and placed four times from nine Goodwood Good-to-Firm runs; a natural prominent racer who will be active in the early stages to secure his preferred position despite the crowded prominent berths, and Murphy's track record here is a significant asset.

runners_data.name: Shafdar
runners_data.note: Has a hood (t) and a wide range of Goodwood form including a win over 8f; David Egan keeps the ride and the 49-day break is the main query — 3 places from 8 similar-going runs is modest but he has genuine ability and could pick up pieces if the race gets messy late.

runners_data.name: Crest Of Fire
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race; Tom Marquand has ridden him before and on Good to Firm Goodwood he can dictate entirely unchallenged — 7 runs from 9 in similar going shows the conditions suit, and his light 3yo weight of 132lbs is a tangible advantage.

runners_data.name: Thinthread
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave on a George Baker-trained 4yo who carries hood (p); a genuine prominent racer whose recent win came over 10f at Sandown Standard — in this 18-runner field he will be competing hard for a prominent slot and the redistribution reflects the traffic he faces, not his intent.

runners_data.name: Great Chieftain
runners_data.note: Oliver Cole's 5yo has run 14 times on Goodwood Good-to-Firm going for five wins and seven places — that is an extraordinary course-and-conditions strike rate; David Probert takes over and he carries hood (b), but being a true prominent type in a race with too many of the same means he may not get the run of things despite the form credentials.

runners_data.name: First Ambition
runners_data.note: Michael Keady's 5yo has modest recent form (placed once in last five, all at Kempton Standard) and the stable is 0/8 over 14 days; a genuine prominent type who is unlikely to get his preferred position in this field and whose form does not encourage at this level regardless.

runners_data.name: Blue Courvoisier
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's 3yo has six runs on Goodwood Good-to-Firm going with two wins and four places — almost identical course-and-going profile to Great Chieftain; Saffie Osborne rides and the step up from 8f to 9f on this favourable track could suit a well-handicapped 3yo on 129lbs.

runners_data.name: Alcaraz
runners_data.note: George Baker's 7yo has hold-up profile and two of his best runs came on Soft, with only one place from 11 similar-going starts; C Y Ho is an unfamiliar booking and 72 days off is the longest absence in the field — hard to get excited about his prospects here.

runners_data.name: Thunder Wonder
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston yard is 4/52 over 14 days and Marco Ghiani rides; all five recent runs are at 9f on Goodwood-type going with one win and two places — the form is modest but the consistency at the trip on this type of ground makes him a realistic each-way player if the race develops late.

races.paceDynamic: Crest Of Fire is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field and, with no rival capable of seriously disputing the lead, Tom Marquand can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on Good To Firm ground over 1m1f at Goodwood. Behind him, Alpha Crucis, Boyfriend, Real Gain, El Matador, Ammes, Spell Master and Blue Courvoisier all want to race prominently, but the field holds far more genuine prominent types than can all secure their natural positions — Sweet Reward, Point Of Contact, Thinthread, Great Chieftain and First Ambition are true prominent racers shuffled back to midfield on the map purely because there is no room. Of those, Sweet Reward (9-year-old who knows his job) and Point Of Contact (Oisin Murphy, strong Goodwood record) are most likely to actually press forward and claw a prominent berth, but they will be doing so against traffic. A single unhurried pace-setter dictating modest fractions on fast ground over a trip that places a premium on cruising speed and a well-timed kick favours horses who can travel fluidly in the first half of the race and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — making prominent-to-midfield racers with clean Goodwood or Good-to-Firm form the most advantaged profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Crest Of Fire Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Crest Of Fire is allowed to set a measured, uncontested tempo and Marquand times the acceleration from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Crest Of Fire dictates from the front, the moderate gallop plays to his stamina and he quickens clear before the closers can get organised; at 3yo on just 132lbs he is well treated against older rivals if permitted a trouble-free lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent runners settles into a rhythm just off Crest Of Fire and the pace proves just strong enough to set up a two-furlong dash.
scenarios.body: Horses racing in second to fourth at a comfortable tempo have first run on the closers and the race develops into a sprint finish among those who tracked the leader; Goodwood specialist profiles and horses proven on fast ground dominate the finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Crest Of Fire's gallop is genuinely slow enough to bunch the field and create a wall of horses turning in, leaving late pace through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A true hold-up horse finding daylight late can mow down tired rivals who used energy fighting for position; the compressed race shape compresses sectionals and rewards a long-striding finisher with a high RPR.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If one or more of the pushed-back prominent types forces an early move to claim a prominent position, lifting the tempo and setting up a late-running finish.
scenarios.body: The scramble for position in the first half burns up the prominent brigade earlier than ideal, and a genuine hold-up horse who avoids the tussle arrives with the strongest late run; this outcome relies on an untidy scenario that the field shape makes possible but not probable.

watchPoints.text: Crest Of Fire and the pack of prominent types — watch the first two furlongs carefully; if any of Sweet Reward, Point Of Contact or Thinthread push forward aggressively to dispute, the "uncontested lead" assumption breaks down entirely and pace dynamics shift against Crest Of Fire.

Boyfriend's course-and-conditions record (14 runs, 2W6P on Goodwood Good-to-Firm) is the standout statistic in the race — if he settles in second or third behind Crest Of Fire with a clear run, he becomes the dominant prominent-pace winner.

Great Chieftain has an equally striking Goodwood Good-to-Firm record (14/15, 5W7P) but will be squeezed wide or back by the sheer volume of prominent rivals — watch where David Probert positions him in the first three furlongs as it will define his chance.

Blue Courvoisier on 129lbs as a 3yo with a perfect 6/6 Goodwood Good-to-Firm course form is the most underappreciated runner in the field if Saffie Osborne can get her into a prominent position — the weight allowance over older rivals is significant.

Rock Of Cashel for Jamie Spencer — watch whether Spencer attempts to make progress down the inner at the two-furlong point; in a compressed 18-runner straight at Goodwood, pockets form quickly and Spencer's ability to find gaps will be the deciding factor in whether this hold-up horse gets a clear shot.
